body:
### [[API connection]]

1. Select **[[Ollama]]**, **[[LM Studio]]**, or **[[OpenAI-compatible]]** for other [[servers]] and [[gateways]]. Enter the [[API base URL]], including `/v1`. Defaults: [[Ollama]] `http://localhost:11434/v1`; [[LM Studio]] `http://localhost:1234/v1`.
2. The [[API]] must expose `GET /v1/models` and [[streaming]] `POST /v1/chat/completions`. Enter its **[[API token]]**; without [[authentication]], use any nonempty value such as `local`.
3. **Requests go directly from the [[browser]].** Allow the [[app’s origin]] in [[CORS]], including `Authorization` and `Content-Type` [[headers]]. [[Browser local-network permissions]] and [[HTTPS/mixed-content restrictions]] also apply.

### [[Web search]]

In the [[provider]]’s **[[Search connection]]** field, choose the [[interface]] your [[server]] supports:

- **[[Server-managed · LM Studio MCP]]:** requires `/api/v1/chat`, [[authenticated MCP access]], and **[[Allow calling servers from mcp.json]]**. Enter the configured [[server name]] without `mcp/`, plus exact allowed [[tool names]].
- **[[Server-managed · Responses + remote MCP]]:** requires `/v1/responses` with [[server-executed MCP]]. Enter the [[search MCP URL]] reachable by that [[server]] and exact allowed [[tool names]]. No separate [[MCP authentication]] field is provided.
- **[[Server-managed · LocalAI]]:** requires [[Chat Completions]] with [[MCP support]]. Enter the [[search-server names]] already configured for the [[model]].
- **[[Browser-managed · SearXNG]]:** enter a [[browser]]-reachable [[SearXNG URL]] with [[JSON]] results and [[CORS]] enabled. Requires [[model tool calling]]. Search requests send no [[credentials]] or [[cookies]].

**Allow only [[read-only search tools]].** Keep [[search-service credentials]] on the [[server]]. **[[Web search off]]** disables app-requested search, not independent search enforced by your [[server]].

### [[Model selection and checks]]

Assign roles in **[[Models and generation]]**. [[Main and secondary models]] require [[vision]] for [[image tasks]]; [[interactive nodes]] also require [[vision]] for screenshot review, plus reliable [[coding]]. [[Tool calling]] is recommended.

If [[capability metadata]] is incomplete, use **[[Show all models]]** for that role. This bypasses [[filtering]] and [[capability checks]], not actual [[API requirements]].

Use **[[Test model capabilities]]** to verify [[output structure]], [[image input]], [[tools]], and search. Tests use your current [[prompts]] and [[token limits]]. Match **[[Generation token limits]]** to your [[server]]’s output and [[context budgets]].

**[[Local image generation]] is not supported.**

previews.api connection: An API connection is a **software communication link** through which the app sends prompts to a model server and receives answers using an agreed **request format**.
previews.openai-compatible: OpenAI-compatible describes an API that follows **OpenAI’s request and response formats**, allowing this app to use another provider’s models through **matching endpoints** without connecting to OpenAI itself.
previews.servers: Servers are **programs that receive requests** and return results over a network, such as model answers or search results, whether running on **your computer or elsewhere**.
previews.gateways: Gateways are **intermediary services** that accept the app’s API requests and **forward them** to model servers, potentially translating formats or managing authentication along the way.
previews.api base url: An API base URL is the **shared starting address** for a server’s API endpoints, including **/v1** here, to which paths such as /models are appended.
previews.api: An API, or application programming interface, is a **set of communication rules** that lets software request another program’s services through defined **operations and data formats**.
previews.streaming: Streaming is the **incremental delivery** of a model’s answer as it is generated, letting the app display text **before the full response finishes**.
previews.api token: An API token is a **credential sent with requests** to gain server access; when this local server requires no authentication, the app still needs a **nonempty placeholder** such as local.
previews.authentication: Authentication is the process of **verifying a requester’s identity** or credentials before granting access, often by checking an **API token** supplied with each request.
previews.browser: A browser is the **web-page software** running the app that, in this setup, sends requests **directly to your model server** rather than through an app-hosted intermediary.
previews.app’s origin: The app’s origin is the combination of its **protocol, hostname, and port**, which the browser uses to identify the requesting website when enforcing **cross-origin access rules**.
previews.cors: CORS is a **browser-enforced access mechanism** through which a server declares which website origins may read its responses and which **request headers** they may send.
previews.headers: Headers are **request or response metadata** sent alongside API content, such as **Authorization and Content-Type**, which carry credentials and identify the format of the transmitted data.
previews.browser local-network permissions: Browser local-network permissions are **browser access controls** that may require your approval before a website can contact services on **your computer or private network**.
previews.https/mixed-content restrictions: HTTPS/mixed-content restrictions are **browser security rules** that can block an encrypted HTTPS app from contacting an **unencrypted HTTP server**, potentially preventing local API connections.
previews.web search: Web search is the **retrieval of online information** through a connected search service, giving models **external results** beyond their training knowledge when the configured interface supports it.
previews.provider: A provider is a **configured source of AI services** that tells the app which server supplies its models and how to **connect and authenticate**.
previews.search connection: Search connection is the **provider setting** that selects how search requests reach a search service, using either **server-managed or browser-managed** execution according to the supported interface.
previews.interface: An interface is an **agreed communication contract** specifying how software exchanges requests and results, such as the **endpoints and message formats** required for a search connection.
previews.server: A server is a **program that handles requests** from other software, supplying services such as model generation or search through **network-accessible addresses**.
previews.server-managed · lm studio mcp: Server-managed · LM Studio MCP is a **search connection mode** where LM Studio’s /api/v1/chat endpoint runs permitted search tools through **Model Context Protocol** using authenticated access and explicitly enabled configured servers.
previews.authenticated mcp access: Authenticated MCP access is a **credential-verified connection** to tools exposed through Model Context Protocol, the communication standard that lets an AI application invoke **external tools** such as search.
previews.ollama: Ollama is a **local AI model runner** that downloads and runs language models on your computer, exposing an **OpenAI-compatible API** so apps can send prompts and receive generated responses.
previews.lm studio: LM Studio is a **desktop application** for downloading and running AI models locally, with a graphical interface and a **built-in API server** that lets other apps use those models.
previews.allow calling servers from mcp.json: “Allow calling servers from mcp.json” is an **LM Studio permission** that lets it invoke **external tools** through servers listed in its mcp.json configuration file.
previews.server name: A server name is the **configured identifier** for an MCP tool service, entered in the LM Studio search connection **without the mcp/ prefix** so requests reach the intended service.
previews.tool names: Tool names are the **exact identifiers** of individual operations offered by a connected service, used here to **limit access** to explicitly permitted search functions.
previews.server-managed · responses + remote mcp: “Server-managed · Responses + remote MCP” is a search connection mode where the provider’s **/v1/responses interface** lets its server invoke **remote search tools** through Model Context Protocol rather than through the browser.
previews.server-executed mcp: Server-executed MCP means the **provider server** invokes external tools through Model Context Protocol, handling **tool communication** rather than leaving those requests to the browser.
previews.search mcp url: A search MCP URL is the **network address** of a search service exposing tools through Model Context Protocol, which must be **reachable by the provider server** in the Responses-based connection.
previews.mcp authentication: MCP authentication is the **identity verification** required to access a Model Context Protocol tool service; this app provides **no separate authentication field** for the Responses-based remote MCP connection.
previews.server-managed · localai: “Server-managed · LocalAI” is a search connection mode that uses **LocalAI’s Chat Completions interface** to invoke MCP search services **already configured for the model** on the server.
previews.chat completions: Chat Completions is an **API interface** that accepts conversation messages and returns a model’s next response, using **/v1/chat/completions** here with streaming output and, for LocalAI search, MCP integration.
previews.mcp support: MCP support is the ability to use **Model Context Protocol**, a shared format for connecting AI systems to external tools, enabling the server to **invoke search services** through its model interface.
previews.search-server names: Search-server names are the **configured identifiers** of search services already attached to a LocalAI model, which the app supplies to select **which services to use**.
previews.model: A model is a **trained AI system** that processes prompts and produces responses, with capabilities such as **image understanding or tool calling** determining which app tasks it can perform.
previews.browser-managed · searxng: “Browser-managed · SearXNG” is a search connection mode where the **browser queries SearXNG directly** for JSON results, requiring model tool calling and **cross-origin access permission** without sending credentials or cookies.
previews.searxng url: A SearXNG URL is the **web address** of a SearXNG search service, which must be browser-reachable and provide **JSON search results** with permission for requests from the app’s origin.
previews.json: JSON is a **text-based data format** that represents information using named fields, lists, and basic values, letting the app **read search results** as structured data rather than a webpage.
previews.model tool calling: Model tool calling is the ability to generate **structured requests** for external functions, such as search, so the surrounding software can **execute the request** and return results to the model.
previews.credentials: Credentials are **authentication details**, such as API tokens or passwords, that prove access rights to a service; browser-managed SearXNG requests **send none** in this app.
previews.cookies: Cookies are **small browser-stored values** that websites use to maintain sessions or preferences; this app **does not send them** with browser-managed SearXNG search requests.
previews.read-only search tools: Read-only search tools are functions that **retrieve information** without modifying external data or taking actions such as posting messages, limiting search access to **non-modifying operations**.
previews.search-service credentials: Search-service credentials are **secrets such as API keys** that authorize access to a search provider and should remain **on the server** rather than being exposed to browser code.
previews.web search off: “Web search off” is a setting that disables **app-requested searches** but does not prevent **independent server searches** performed under the provider server’s own configuration.
previews.model selection and checks: Model selection and checks is the process of **assigning AI models to tasks** and testing whether they meet requirements such as image input, tool use, and **correct output structure**.
previews.models and generation: “Models and generation” is the **settings area** for assigning models to app roles and configuring **response generation**, including token limits that must fit the server’s capacity.
previews.main and secondary models: Main and secondary models are **AI model assignments** for primary and supporting app roles, and **both require image-understanding capability** when their tasks involve images.
previews.vision: Vision is a model’s ability to **interpret images** alongside text, enabling it to answer questions about **visual content** such as objects, diagrams, or screenshots.
previews.image tasks: Image tasks are requests that require **understanding visual input**, such as describing a photograph or reading a chart, so the assigned model needs **vision support** rather than text-only processing.
previews.interactive nodes: Interactive nodes are **self-contained programs**, such as simulations and calculators, whose generation uses **coding, behavior checks, and screenshot review**.
previews.coding: Coding is **writing computer instructions** to implement behavior, with interactive nodes requiring models that can produce **reliable code** rather than merely describe what should happen.
previews.tool calling: Tool calling is a model’s ability to request **external functions** using structured names and arguments, letting the app or server perform actions such as **web searches** beyond generating text.
previews.capability metadata: Capability metadata is **descriptive information** supplied about a model’s supported features, such as vision or tool calling, which the app uses to determine **role eligibility** but which may be incomplete.
previews.show all models: Show all models is an option that reveals models normally excluded from a role by **capability filtering**, allowing selection despite incomplete metadata without removing the server’s **actual technical requirements**.
previews.filtering: Filtering is the app’s **narrowing of model choices** for a role based on reported capabilities, keeping models without the expected features out of the **displayed selection**.
previews.capability checks: Capability checks are app-level evaluations of whether a model supports a role’s **required features**, which Show all models can bypass without making an **unsupported feature** work.
previews.api requirements: API requirements are the **technical conditions** a server must meet for requests to work, including required endpoints, authentication, and streaming support, regardless of **model-selection overrides**.
previews.test model capabilities: Test model capabilities is a **verification feature** that tries output formatting, image input, tool use, and search using your **current prompts and token limits** rather than relying only on model descriptions.
previews.output structure: Output structure is the **organization and formatting** of a model’s response, such as required fields in a machine-readable object, which must match what the **app expects** to process reliably.
previews.image input: Image input is **visual data** sent to a model as part of a request, requiring both the server and model to support **image processing** rather than text alone.
previews.tools: Tools are **callable functions** available through the app or server that perform tasks outside text generation, such as retrieving search results, when a model issues a **structured request**.
previews.prompts: Prompts are the **instructions and information** given to a model to guide its response, with capability tests using your **current prompt settings** so results reflect that configuration.
previews.token limits: Token limits are **size caps** measured in chunks of text called tokens, restricting how much a model can receive or generate according to the **specific limit** being configured.
previews.generation token limits: Generation token limits are settings that cap the **amount of model output** per response and must fit the server’s supported output allowance and **available context space**.
previews.context budgets: Context budgets are the **available token capacity** for material a model processes in one request, with input and generated output needing to fit within the server’s **applicable limits**.
previews.local image generation: Local image generation means using a **locally running model** to create new images from instructions, a feature this app **does not support**, distinct from analyzing images supplied as input.

editorialNote: Screenshot-review requirements updated manually; existing model-generated term markings and other previews retained.
